title: fix(components): recompile a react page on its content, not its schema identity
body:
Fixes #13268
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ReactKindPage` (`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx`) built its compile scope in a `useMemo` keyed on `[schema, adapter]`. `ReactRunner` recompiles whenever the scope identity changes, and every compile mints a new `Page` function, so a new schema object with the same content remounted the page and wiped its `useState`. The console's `PageView` hands `SchemaRenderer` a fresh spread of the page on every render, so any `PageView` re-render reset a react page (measured on the showcase Task Desk: `editId` reset and the open record drawer vanished).

The scope is now rebuilt only when what it is compiled from changes:

- the schema's **content**, compared structurally by a file-local `sameContent` helper (plain objects and arrays by their own keys, everything else by `Object.is`, cycle-safe). `page` in the scope carries the whole schema, so this covers `source`, `data`, `variables`, and every other page value the page can read (`context.params` included);
- the adapter, by identity (unchanged; the reason it stays a recompile trigger is kept in the comment).

The cached scope lives in `useState` and is replaced during render when the content moves (React's documented shape for state derived from props), not in a `useMemo`: React may discard a memo, and here a new object is a remount (AGENTS.md #10). A first draft held it in a ref; `react-hooks/refs` flags reading a ref during render, so it moved to state.

## Seam chosen, and why

`ReactKindPage`, not `PageView`. The defect is that the page keys its compile on identity; any host can hand it a fresh object, and `PageView` is only the one measured. Stabilising `PageView`'s spread would fix that host and leave the contract identity-sensitive for every other. `PageView.tsx` is untouched; StrictMode is untouched; `PageView` re-renders are not suppressed. No new export or prop.

## Pins (`packages/components/src/__tests__/react-page-content-identity.test.tsx`, all under `React.StrictMode`)

- (a) a react page with `useState` set by a click keeps it across two host re-renders that each hand it a new but equal schema object;
- (b) CONTROL: a changed `source` recompiles and the page resets;
- (c) CONTROL: a changed declared scope value (`variables.greeting`) recompiles, the new value reaches the page, and the page resets. Measured: scope values are compiled in, not passed as props, so a value change reaches the page only through a recompile;
- (c2) CONTROL: a changed nested page value (`context.params`) recompiles too.

`react-page-state.test.tsx` already had "survives a parent re-render", but its host re-renders with a module-scope schema, the one shape a real host does not produce; its header comment is updated to the new keying.

- Ablation on the final implementation (head `c016ba798f`), via `ablation-replace.mjs`: `!sameContent(compiled.schema, schema)` replaced by `compiled.schema !== schema` (anchor x1 to x0, blob `149963d2927e` to `16dddb7d4244`); (a) went red, `Tests 1 failed | 3 passed (4)`. Restored by the tool's trap: blob after restore `149963d2927e6dc51a1ff183e1ca24863ab6e077` equals the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty. The test imports the renderer through `../renderers` (source), so no build was in the path.

- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 3 changed TS files: 0 errors. `react-page.tsx` warnings: the same six pre-existing `no-explicit-any` as base, minus the base's `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` (the memo it sat on is gone).

Declared to CI: the full `packages/components/` directory (no whole-directory run here; the container's test lock is shared).

## Acceptance notes

- `PageView.tsx` still hands a fresh spread every render. That is now harmless to react pages; other blocks under it are not in this card's scope.
- A host that puts a non-plain value (a function, a `Date`) in the page schema and hands a new one every render will still recompile each time: `sameContent` compares such values by identity, the conservative answer. Whether any producer of page metadata does that was not searched.
